An execution plan is the Directed Acyclic Graph that Tabsdata automatically builds whenever a function is triggered. Rather than running only the function you triggered, Tabsdata follows the data dependencies to work out every other function that has to run as a result, and puts them in the order those dependencies require. A single plan can cross several collections.

Secret class class Secret(value: str | None = None) Categories: credentials Reference to a secret value, used for credential fields. A Secret is either hydrated -- Secret("hunter2"), whose value() returns the value -- or dehydrated -- Secret(), whose value() raises. None is the dehydrated sentinel and is never a valid value. It always serializes to the redacted marker ":secret:", so the value never lands in the serialized form and str(secret) is always redacted.

StrOrSecretSpec type_alias StrOrSecretSpec: Union[str, Secret] Resolved type: str | Secret Categories: credentials A connector field that accepts either a plain string or a Secret. Annotate a connection/source/destination field with it directly. Each value carries a marker so the two shapes are unambiguous on the wire: "str:<value>" -- a plain string (<value> may be empty); "secret:<value>" -- a secret carrying <value>; ":secret:" -- a secret with no value yet (resolved at run time). An unmarked string is rejected. After validation a plain arm is a str and a secret arm a Secret, so read the value with a normal str or with Secret.value() respectively. Connector code that must resolve either arm to a concrete value uses the connector-common _convert helper.

Write a table to a single Parquet file, one slot per path: @subscriber( destination=AzureBlobDest( paths=["exports/rows.parquet"], format=DestFileFormat.PARQUET, ), input_tables=["mycoll/rows"], ) def publish(rows: TableFrameSpec) -> TableFrameSpec: return rows Write CSV and tune the writer through format_cfg, keyed by the DestFileFormat: @subscriber( destination=AzureBlobDest( paths=["exports/rows.csv"], format=DestFileFormat.CSV, format_cfg={ DestFileFormat.CSV: { "separator": ";", "include_header": True, }, }, ), input_tables=["mycoll/rows"], ) def publish(rows: TableFrameSpec) -> TableFrameSpec: return rows

class class MongoDBDest( collections_with_ids: CollectionsWithIdsSpec, if_collection_exists: IfTableExistsSpec = 'append', use_trxs: bool = False, docs_per_trx: int = 1000, maintain_order: bool = False, update_existing: bool = True, fail_on_duplicate_key: bool = True, log_intermediate_files: bool = False, dest_cfg: DestCfgSpec | None = None, ) Bases: Dest Categories: destination MongoDB destination for @subscriber -- one slot per collection.

Append documents, letting MongoDB auto-generate _id (the id field is None): @subscriber( destination=MongoDBDest( collections_with_ids=[("cap_append", None)], ), input_tables=["caps_input/cap_rows"], ) def publish(rows: TableFrameSpec) -> TableFrameSpec: return rows Upsert on a natural key -- code becomes each document's _id, so re-runs update the same documents instead of inserting duplicates: @subscriber( destination=MongoDBDest( collections_with_ids=[("cap_upsert", "code")], update_existing=True, ), input_tables=["caps_input/cap_rows"], ) def upsert(rows: TableFrameSpec) -> TableFrameSpec: return rows

parameter collections_with_idsCollectionsWithIdsSpec (list[tuple[str, str | None]]) List of (collection, id_field) pairs, one write slot per entry. collection is the target collection, optionally qualified as <database>.<collection>; a bare <collection> targets the database named in the connection URI (a name up to 235 bytes, no NUL or $, not starting with system.). id_field is the document field used as the unique id, e.g. ("mydb.users", "user_id"); pass None (e.g. ("mydb.logs", None)) to let MongoDB auto-generate _id. An id_field may not be empty, contain . or NUL, or start with $.
parameter if_collection_existsIfTableExistsSpec (Literal['append', 'replace']) "append" (default) leaves existing documents in place; "replace" drops the collection first.
parameter use_trxsbool When true, each batch of docs_per_trx documents is wrapped in a MongoDB transaction (requires a replica set).
parameter docs_per_trxint Max documents per write batch / transaction (default 1000; must be greater than 0).
parameter maintain_orderbool When true, documents are inserted in input order (slower but deterministic server-side ordering).

parameter update_existingbool When true, documents whose id already exists are upserted (UpdateOne with upsert=True); when false, InsertOne is used and a collision aborts the batch. Ignored when id_field is None (auto-generated ids never collide).
parameter fail_on_duplicate_keybool When true, a duplicate-key error is re-raised; when false it is logged and the batch continues.
parameter log_intermediate_filesbool When true, each intermediate JSONL chunk written to the work dir is logged before upload -- useful for debugging large writes.

parameter dest_cfgDestCfgSpec | None (Mapping[Literal['mongodb.logging_level'], Any] | None) Optional connector config over the single key mongodb.logging_level. Note: pymongo.* options are read from the connection's conn_cfg, not here.
method validate def validate() Validate that docs_per_trx is positive. Called by the framework; raises MongoDBValidateException.

Data class class Data(df: Any, chunk_size: int | None = None) Categories: source One dataframe emitted by DataGenSrc, optionally chunked. A Data wraps a Polars or Pandas dataframe (a Pandas frame is converted to Polars on construction) plus a per-run chunk_size: chunk_size=None -- the whole dataframe is emitted on every run. chunk_size=N -- N rows are emitted per run, advancing an offset kept in the plugin's per-flow state; once the offset reaches the end the slot yields None (no more rows). On the wire a Data serialises to {"parquet": <base64>, "chunk_size": <int|null>}: the dataframe is written to parquet and base64-encoded on serialisation, and decoded back to a Polars frame on deserialisation so the plugin can materialise it to parquet for its output. Like Secret, it round-trips via its own pydantic core schema rather than the descriptor envelope.

Publish multiple Db2 tables, one output slot per query in order: @publisher( source=Db2Src( queries=[ "SELECT * FROM wld_country", "SELECT * FROM wld_city", ], ), output_tables=["d2_country", "d2_city"], ) def ingest(country: TableFrameSpec, city: TableFrameSpec): return country, city Incremental read: an initial_values bind seeds the :wm watermark on the first run, then ctx advances it each run. Db2 folds unquoted identifiers to uppercase, so the column is ID: @publisher( source=Db2Src( queries=[ "SELECT * FROM wld_city WHERE id > :wm " "ORDER BY id FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY" ], initial_values={"wm": 0}, ), output_tables=["d2_city_inc"], ) def ingest_inc(city: TableFrameSpec, ctx: TrxCtx): if city is not None: row = city.max_for("ID") if row is not None and row["ID"] is not None: ctx.set_attr("wm", int(row["ID"])) return city

Each name is bound into the query as a SQLAlchemy :var parameter at execute time, and acts as the first-run seed: the plugin reads ctx.get_attr(bind_name) per bind and falls back to this value when the ctx store has no entry. FETCH NEXT (which needs ORDER BY); an initial_values bind seeds :wm on the first run and ctx advances it each run: @publisher( source=MSSQLSrc( queries=[ "SELECT * FROM wld_city WHERE id > :wm " "ORDER BY id OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY" ], initial_values={"wm": 0}, ), output_tables=["ms_city_inc"], ) def ingest_inc(city: TableFrameSpec, ctx: TrxCtx): if city is not None: row = city.max_for("id") if row is not None and row["id"] is not None: ctx.set_attr("wm", int(row["id"])) return city

StreamStageSrcPlugin class class StreamStageSrcPlugin Bases: SrcPlugin Categories: spi Hidden batch-side (publisher) source that ingests a stream stage's manifests. A StreamSrcPlugin only stages data (accumulates batches into storage and records each in a manifest); every StreamSrc needs a paired hidden SrcPlugin on the batch side to consume it, which must be this class or a subclass. Each execution consumes exactly one manifest -- the oldest unconsumed one -- advancing a per-flow cursor; it yields zero output slots when none remain. The manifest scan + ingest is fixed in read_in and must not be overridden; customise the ingested data (e.g. de-duplication) by overriding process_files instead. To register a customised variant, pair a StreamStageSrc subclass with this plugin in a SrcDef whose cardinality returns -1 (disables the slot-count check) and whose explorer is None.

LazyGroupBy class class LazyGroupBy(lgb, parent, by) Categories: aggregation Pending group-by over a TableFrame, produced by group_by. Obtain one from TableFrame.group_by(...), then call .agg(...) with reducing expressions such as col("v").sum(). The reduction shortcut methods (sum / min / max / mean / median / n_unique) reduce EVERY column and can fail on a table's hidden system columns; prefer agg(col(...).<reduction>()). count and len are always safe.

method agg def agg( *aggs: IntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] = (), **named_aggs: IntoExpr = {}, ) -> TableFrame Reduce each group to one row using the given expressions. Each expression is a column reduction -- typically col(name) plus a reducer and an alias. The result has one row per group: the group key column(s) followed by the aggregated columns. Parameters: # parameter *aggsIntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Iterable[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None]) Aggregation expressions to compute per group. # parameter **named_aggsIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Aggregation expressions as keyword arguments, where the keyword names the output column. Example: tf.group_by("k").agg(col("v").sum().alias("s")) tf.group_by("k").agg(col("v").mean().alias("m"))

method len def len(name: str | None = None) -> TableFrame Count the rows in each group. Safe on any TableFrame (it counts rows, not column values). Parameters: # parameter namestr | None Name for the count column (default "len"). Example: tf.group_by("g").len() Name the output column to keep it distinct from the data: tf.group_by("g").len("rows")

method count def count() -> TableFrame Count the non-null values of each column within each group. Yields one count column per non-key column. Safe on any TableFrame (it counts values, not reduces them). Example: tf.group_by("g").count()

method max def max() -> TableFrame Take the maximum of each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).max()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").max().alias("largest"))

method mean def mean() -> TableFrame Average each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).mean()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").mean().alias("average"))

method median def median() -> TableFrame Take the median of each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).median()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").median().alias("middle"))

method min def min() -> TableFrame Take the minimum of each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).min()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").min().alias("smallest"))

method n_unique def n_unique() -> TableFrame Count the distinct values of each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).n_unique()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").n_unique().alias("distinct"))

method sum def sum() -> TableFrame Sum each non-key column within each group. Reduces EVERY column; may fail on a table's hidden system columns through storage. Prefer agg(col(...).sum()). Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").sum().alias("total"))

class class ColumnDefinition(name: str | None = None, dtype: ColumnDataType = String) Categories: projection, string The column one Grok capture produces: its name and data type. One of these per capture makes up the schema passed to TableFrame.grok, keyed by capture name. The captured text is parsed into dtype; a row that does not match leaves the column null.

tf.grok( "logs", r"%{WORD:user}-%{INT:year}", { "user": ColumnDefinition("user", String), "year": ColumnDefinition("year", Int64), }, ) A name that differs from the capture renames the column it produces -- here the user capture lands in a column called who: tf.grok( "logs", r"%{WORD:user}-.*", {"user": ColumnDefinition("who", String)}, )
parameter namestr | None Name of the column to add. None (the default) keeps the capture's own name, and any other value renames it.

parameter dtypeColumnDataType (DataType | DataTypeClass) Data type the captured text is parsed into, from tabsdatak.tableframe.datatypes -- a type (Int64) or an instance where it is parameterized (Datetime("us")). Defaults to String, which keeps the text as captured.
ExprStringNameSpace class class ExprStringNameSpace Categories: string String methods, accessed via Expr.str.
class class ExprStringNameSpace Categories: string String methods, accessed via Expr.str.
tf.with_columns(col("name").str.to_uppercase().alias("upper"))

method to_date def to_date( format: str | None = None, *, strict: bool = True, exact: bool = True, cache: bool = True, ) -> Expr Parse each string into a date. Parameters: # parameter formatstr | None chrono-style date format (e.g. %Y-%m-%d); inferred when omitted. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an unparseable string; if False, set it to null. # parameter exactbool If True, the whole string must match; if False, match a date found anywhere in it. # parameter cachebool Cache parsing of repeated strings. Example: tf.select(col("day").str.to_date("%Y-%m-%d").alias("date")) Omit the format to have it inferred, and pass strict=False to null out the strings that do not parse: tf.select(col("day").str.to_date(strict=False).alias("date"))

method to_datetime def to_datetime( format: str | None = None, *, time_unit: TimeUnit | None = None, time_zone: str | None = None, strict: bool = True, exact: bool = True, cache: bool = True, ambiguous: Ambiguous | Expr = 'raise', ) -> Expr Parse each string into a datetime. Parameters: # parameter formatstr | None chrono-style datetime format; inferred when omitted. # parameter time_unitTimeUnit | None (Literal['ns', 'us', 'ms'] | None) Resolution of the result: ns, us or ms. # parameter time_zonestr | None Time zone to attach to the result. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an unparseable string; if False, set it to null. # parameter exactbool If True, the whole string must match; if False, match a datetime found anywhere in it. # parameter cachebool Cache parsing of repeated strings. # parameter ambiguousAmbiguous | Expr (Literal['earliest', 'latest', 'raise', 'null'] | Expr) Policy for ambiguous local times: earliest, latest, raise or null. Example: tf.select(col("when").str.to_datetime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))

method to_time def to_time( format: str | None = None, *, strict: bool = True, cache: bool = True, ) -> Expr Parse each string into a time. Parameters: # parameter formatstr | None chrono-style time format (e.g. %H:%M:%S); inferred when omitted. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an unparseable string; if False, set it to null. # parameter cachebool Cache parsing of repeated strings. Example: tf.select(col("clock").str.to_time("%H:%M:%S").alias("time"))
method len_bytes def len_bytes() -> Expr Number of bytes in each string (not characters). Example: tf.select(col("name").str.len_bytes().alias("bytes"))
method len_chars def len_chars() -> Expr Number of characters in each string (not bytes). Example: tf.select(col("name").str.len_chars().alias("chars"))
method to_uppercase def to_uppercase() -> Expr Convert each string to uppercase. Example: tf.with_columns(col("name").str.to_uppercase().alias("upper"))
method to_lowercase def to_lowercase() -> Expr Convert each string to lowercase. Example: tf.with_columns(col("name").str.to_lowercase().alias("lower"))
method to_titlecase def to_titlecase() -> Expr Title-case each string, capitalizing the first letter of a word. Example: tf.with_columns(col("name").str.to_titlecase().alias("title"))

method strip_chars def strip_chars(characters: IntoExpr = None) -> Expr Trim the given characters from both ends of each string. Parameters: # parameter charactersIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Set of characters to remove, in any order; whitespace when omitted. Example: tf.with_columns(col("name").str.strip_chars().alias("trimmed")) Pass the characters to remove to strip something other than whitespace: tf.select(col("email").str.strip_chars(".moc").alias("stripped"))

method strip_chars_start def strip_chars_start(characters: IntoExpr = None) -> Expr Trim the given characters from the start of each string. Parameters: # parameter charactersIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Set of characters to remove, in any order; whitespace when omitted. Example: tf.select(col("name").str.strip_chars_start().alias("lstripped"))

method strip_chars_end def strip_chars_end(characters: IntoExpr = None) -> Expr Trim the given characters from the end of each string. Parameters: # parameter charactersIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Set of characters to remove, in any order; whitespace when omitted. Example: tf.select(col("name").str.strip_chars_end().alias("rstripped"))

method strip_prefix def strip_prefix(prefix: IntoExpr) -> Expr Remove prefix from the start of each string if present. Parameters: # parameter prefixIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Exact prefix to remove. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.strip_prefix("ada").alias("rest"))

method strip_suffix def strip_suffix(suffix: IntoExpr) -> Expr Remove suffix from the end of each string if present. Parameters: # parameter suffixIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Exact suffix to remove. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.strip_suffix(".com").alias("rest"))

method pad_start def pad_start(length: int | IntoExprColumn, fill_char: str = ' ') -> Expr Left-pad each string to length with a fill character. Strings already at or over length are unchanged. Parameters: # parameter lengthint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Target length. # parameter fill_charstr Single character used for padding. Example: tf.select(col("qty").str.pad_start(6, "-").alias("padded"))

method pad_end def pad_end(length: int | IntoExprColumn, fill_char: str = ' ') -> Expr Right-pad each string to length with a fill character. Strings already at or over length are unchanged. Parameters: # parameter lengthint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Target length. # parameter fill_charstr Single character used for padding. Example: tf.select(col("qty").str.pad_end(6, "-").alias("padded"))

method zfill def zfill(length: int | IntoExprColumn) -> Expr Left-pad each numeric string with zeros to length. A leading sign is preserved before the zeros. Strings already at or over length are unchanged. Parameters: # parameter lengthint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Target length. Example: tf.select(col("qty").str.zfill(5).alias("padded")) # "42" -> "00042"

method contains def contains(pattern: str | Expr, *, literal: bool = False, strict: bool = True) -> Expr Return whether each string contains pattern. Parameters: # parameter patternstr | Expr Regular expression, or a literal when literal is True. # parameter literalbool Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an invalid regex. Example: tf.filter(col("email").str.contains("@example")) The pattern is a regular expression unless literal is set: tf.filter(col("email").str.contains(".com", literal=True))

method find def find(pattern: str | Expr, *, literal: bool = False, strict: bool = True) -> Expr Return the index of the first match of pattern, or null. Parameters: # parameter patternstr | Expr Regular expression, or a literal when literal is True. # parameter literalbool Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an invalid regex. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.find("@").alias("at"))

method ends_with def ends_with(suffix: str | Expr) -> Expr Return whether each string ends with suffix. Parameters: # parameter suffixstr | Expr Literal suffix to test for. Example: tf.filter(col("email").str.ends_with(".com"))

method starts_with def starts_with(prefix: str | Expr) -> Expr Return whether each string starts with prefix. Parameters: # parameter prefixstr | Expr Literal prefix to test for. Example: tf.filter(col("email").str.starts_with("ada"))

method extract def extract(pattern: IntoExprColumn, group_index: int = 1) -> Expr Extract a regex capture group from each string. Returns null where the pattern does not match. Parameters: # parameter patternIntoExprColumn (Expr | str) Regular expression with one or more capture groups. # parameter group_indexint 1-based group to return; 0 returns the whole match. Example: col("email").str.extract(r"(.+)@(.+)", 2) # the domain

method count_matches def count_matches(pattern: str | Expr, *, literal: bool = False) -> Expr Count non-overlapping matches of pattern in each string. Parameters: # parameter patternstr | Expr Regular expression, or a literal when literal is True. # parameter literalbool Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex. Example: tf.select( col("email").str.count_matches(".", literal=True).alias("dots"), )

method replace def replace( pattern: str | Expr, value: str | Expr, *, literal: bool = False, n: int = 1, ) -> Expr Replace matches of pattern with value in each string. Parameters: # parameter patternstr | Expr Regular expression, or a literal when literal is True. # parameter valuestr | Expr Replacement string; may reference capture groups. # parameter literalbool Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex. # parameter nint Number of matches to replace, counted from the left. Example: tf.with_columns(col("email").str.replace("example", "acme")) Only the first match is replaced; use replace_all for every match: tf.select(col("email").str.replace(r"[aeiou]", "*").alias("masked"))

method replace_all def replace_all( pattern: str | Expr, value: str | Expr, *, literal: bool = False, ) -> Expr Replace all matches of pattern with value in each string. Parameters: # parameter patternstr | Expr Regular expression, or a literal when literal is True. # parameter valuestr | Expr Replacement string; may reference capture groups. # parameter literalbool Treat pattern as a literal string, not a regex. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.replace_all(r"[aeiou]", "*"))
method reverse def reverse() -> Expr Reverse the characters of each string. Example: tf.select(col("name").str.reverse().alias("reversed"))

method slice def slice( offset: int | IntoExprColumn, length: int | IntoExprColumn | None = None, ) -> Expr Extract a substring at an offset for a given length. Parameters: # parameter offsetint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Start index; a negative value counts from the end. # parameter lengthint | IntoExprColumn | None (int | Expr | str | None) Number of characters; to the end of the string when omitted. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.slice(0, 3).alias("prefix")) A negative offset counts from the end of the string: tf.select(col("email").str.slice(-3).alias("tld"))

method head def head(n: int | IntoExprColumn) -> Expr Return the first n characters of each string. Parameters: # parameter nint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Number of leading characters; a negative value drops that many from the end. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.head(3).alias("first_three"))

method tail def tail(n: int | IntoExprColumn) -> Expr Return the last n characters of each string. Parameters: # parameter nint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Number of trailing characters; a negative value drops that many from the start. Example: tf.select(col("email").str.tail(3).alias("last_three"))

method to_integer def to_integer( *, base: int | IntoExprColumn = 10, dtype: PolarsIntegerType = Int64, strict: bool = True, ) -> Expr Parse each string into an integer. #MANUAL CHANGE POST GEN: default dtype is the Tabsdata alias Int64 from tabsdatak.tableframe.datatypes (import added); the generated stub referenced a bare, unimported Int64. Parameters: # parameter baseint | IntoExprColumn (int | Expr | str) Numeric base for parsing (e.g. 10, 2, 16). # parameter dtypePolarsIntegerType (type[Any]) Target integer type -- a Tabsdata datatype (e.g. Int64, Int32, UInt16), not a raw polars one. # parameter strictbool If True, raise on an unparseable string; if False, set it to null. Example: tf.select(col("qty").str.to_integer().alias("count")) Parse in another base, or widen the result type: tf.select(col("qty").str.to_integer(base=16, dtype=Int32))

method contains_any def contains_any(patterns: IntoExpr, *, ascii_case_insensitive: bool = False) -> Expr Return whether each string contains any of the patterns. Parameters: # parameter patternsIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Collection of substrings to search for. # parameter ascii_case_insensitivebool Match ASCII letters case-insensitively. Example: tf.filter(col("email").str.contains_any(["example", "navy"]))

method replace_many def replace_many( patterns: IntoExpr | Mapping[str, str], replace_with: IntoExpr = ..., *, ascii_case_insensitive: bool = False, leftmost: bool = False, ) -> Expr Replace all occurrences of many substrings at once. Parameters: # parameter patternsIntoExpr | Mapping[str, str] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Mapping[str, str]) Substrings to replace, or a {pattern: replacement} mapping. # parameter replace_withIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Replacement for each pattern, matched by position; omit when patterns is a mapping. # parameter ascii_case_insensitivebool Match ASCII letters case-insensitively. # parameter leftmostbool Match the leftmost pattern instead of the longest. Example: col("email").str.replace_many({"example": "acme", ".com": ".io"})

Expr class class Expr Categories: tableframe A lazy column expression evaluated against a TableFrame. Create expressions with col / lit from tabsdatak.tableframe.functions and pass them to a frame's select, filter, with_columns or group_by().agg. Operators are element-wise; reducers (sum, mean, min ...) collapse a group. Date/time and string helpers live under dt and str.

class class Expr Categories: tableframe A lazy column expression evaluated against a TableFrame. Create expressions with col / lit from tabsdatak.tableframe.functions and pass them to a frame's select, filter, with_columns or group_by().agg. Operators are element-wise; reducers (sum, mean, min ...) collapse a group. Date/time and string helpers live under dt and str.
tf.with_columns((col("a") * 2).alias("doubled")) tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").sum().alias("total"))
property dtExprDateTimeNameSpace Namespace of date and time operations for temporal columns.
property strExprStringNameSpace Namespace of string operations for string columns.
method sqrt def sqrt() -> Expr Square root of each element. Example: tf.select(col("v").sqrt().alias("root"))
method cbrt def cbrt() -> Expr Cube root of each element. Example: tf.select(col("v").cbrt().alias("root"))
method log10 def log10() -> Expr Base-10 logarithm of each element. Example: tf.select(col("v").log10().alias("magnitude"))
method exp def exp() -> Expr Exponential (e raised to each element). Example: tf.select(col("v").exp().alias("growth"))

method alias def alias(name: Any) -> Expr Rename the output column of this expression. Parameters: # parameter nameAny New column name. Must be a valid identifier (letters, digits, underscores; starting with a letter or underscore) up to 100 characters. Example: tf.select(col("a").alias("identifier")) An expression keeps no name of its own, so alias every computed column: tf.with_columns((col("a") * 2).alias("doubled"))
method not_ def not_() -> Expr Logical negation of a boolean expression. Example: tf.filter(col("flag").not_())
method is_null def is_null() -> Expr Return whether each element is null. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_null())
method is_not_null def is_not_null() -> Expr Return whether each element is not null. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_not_null())
method is_finite def is_finite() -> Expr Return whether each floating-point element is finite. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_finite())
method is_infinite def is_infinite() -> Expr Return whether each floating-point element is infinite. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_infinite())
method is_nan def is_nan() -> Expr Return whether each floating-point element is NaN. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_nan())
method is_not_nan def is_not_nan() -> Expr Return whether each floating-point element is not NaN. Example: tf.filter(col("v").is_not_nan())
method count def count() -> Expr Count the non-null elements in the group; see len. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("v").count().alias("filled"))
method len def len() -> Expr Count all rows in the group, including nulls; see count. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("v").len().alias("rows"))

method slice def slice(offset: int | Expr, length: int | Expr | None = None) -> Expr Take a contiguous slice of the column's values. Parameters: # parameter offsetint | Expr Start index; a negative value counts from the end. # parameter lengthint | Expr | None Number of values to take; all remaining if omitted. Example: tf.select(col("a").slice(1, 2)) A negative offset counts from the end: tf.select(col("a").slice(-2)) # the last two values
method floor def floor() -> Expr Round each element down to the nearest integer. Example: tf.select(col("v").floor().alias("floor"))
method ceil def ceil() -> Expr Round each element up to the nearest integer. Example: tf.select(col("v").ceil().alias("ceil"))

method round def round(decimals: int = 0, mode: RoundMode = 'half_to_even') -> Expr Round floating-point elements to a number of decimals. Parameters: # parameter decimalsint Number of decimal places to keep; non-negative. # parameter modeRoundMode (Literal['half_to_even', 'half_away_from_zero', 'to_zero']) Tie-breaking rule, one of half_to_even, half_away_from_zero or to_zero. Example: tf.select(col("v").round(2).alias("rounded"))

method round_sig_figs def round_sig_figs(digits: int) -> Expr Round elements to a number of significant figures. Parameters: # parameter digitsint Number of significant figures to keep; positive. Example: tf.select(col("v").round_sig_figs(2).alias("approx"))

method cast def cast( dtype: PolarsDataType | type[Any], *, strict: bool = True, wrap_numerical: bool = False, ) -> Expr Cast the expression to a different data type. Parameters: # parameter dtypePolarsDataType | type[Any] (DataType | type[Any]) Target data type (e.g. pl.Int64, pl.Float64, pl.String). # parameter strictbool If True, raise on values that do not fit the target; if False, set them to null instead. # parameter wrap_numericalbool If True, wrap on numeric overflow rather than raising. Example: tf.select(col("a").cast(Float64)) With strict=False an unconvertible value becomes null instead of raising: tf.select(col("name").cast(Int64, strict=False))

method fill_null def fill_null( value: Any | Expr | None = None, strategy: FillNullStrategy | None = None, limit: int | None = None, ) -> Expr Replace null values with a value or a fill strategy. Pass either value or strategy, not both. Parameters: # parameter valueAny | Expr | None Value or expression to substitute for nulls. # parameter strategyFillNullStrategy | None (Literal['forward', 'backward', 'min', 'max', 'mean', 'zero', 'one'] | None) Fill strategy instead of value: one of forward, backward, min, max, mean, zero or one. # parameter limitint | None Maximum consecutive nulls to fill with forward or backward. Example: tf.with_columns(col("v").fill_null(0.0)) A strategy fills from the neighbouring rows instead of a constant: tf.sort("id").with_columns(col("v").fill_null(strategy="forward"))

method fill_nan def fill_nan(value: int | float | Expr | None) -> Expr Replace NaN values with the given value. Only affects NaN, not null. Use fill_null for nulls. Parameters: # parameter valueint | float | Expr | None Value or expression to substitute for NaN. Example: tf.with_columns(col("v").fill_nan(0.0))
method max def max() -> Expr Return the maximum element in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").max().alias("largest"))
method min def min() -> Expr Return the minimum element in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").min().alias("smallest"))
method sum def sum() -> Expr Return the sum of the elements in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").sum().alias("total"))
method mean def mean() -> Expr Return the mean of the elements in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").mean().alias("average"))
method median def median() -> Expr Return the median of the elements in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").median().alias("middle"))
method n_unique def n_unique() -> Expr Count the distinct elements in the group. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg(col("a").n_unique().alias("distinct"))

method first def first(*, ignore_nulls: bool = False) -> Expr Return the first element in the group. Parameters: # parameter ignore_nullsbool If True, return the first non-null element. Example: tf.sort("id").group_by("g").agg(col("a").first().alias("earliest"))

method last def last(*, ignore_nulls: bool = False) -> Expr Return the last element in the group. Parameters: # parameter ignore_nullsbool If True, return the last non-null element. Example: tf.sort("id").group_by("g").agg(col("a").last().alias("latest"))
method is_unique def is_unique() -> Expr Return whether each element occurs only once in the column. Example: tf.filter(col("g").is_unique())

method filter def filter( *predicates: IntoExprColumn | Iterable[IntoExprColumn] = (), **constraints: Any = {}, ) -> Expr Keep only the values that satisfy the given predicates. Values whose predicate is not True (including null) are dropped. Typically used inside an aggregation. Parameters: # parameter *predicatesIntoExprColumn | Iterable[IntoExprColumn] (Expr | str | Iterable[Expr | str]) Boolean expressions to apply. # parameter **constraintsAny column=value keyword filters, combined with predicates using logical and. Example: tf.group_by("g").agg( col("a").filter(col("a") > 1).sum().alias("big_total"), )

method and_ def and_(*others: Any = ()) -> Expr Bitwise and with the given expressions (integer or boolean). Parameters: # parameter *othersAny Expressions to combine with logical/bitwise and. Example: tf.filter(col("flag").and_(col("a") > 2))

method or_ def or_(*others: Any = ()) -> Expr Bitwise or with the given expressions (integer or boolean). Parameters: # parameter *othersAny Expressions to combine with logical/bitwise or. Example: tf.filter(col("flag").or_(col("a") > 3))

method eq def eq(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise equality, equivalent to expr == other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. A null on either side yields null; use eq_missing to treat two nulls as equal. Example: tf.filter(col("g").eq("x"))

method eq_missing def eq_missing(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise equality where two nulls compare as equal. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.select(col("v").eq(None).alias("eq")) # null everywhere tf.select(col("v").eq_missing(None).alias("eq_missing")) # True on nulls

method ge def ge(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise greater-than-or-equal, like expr >= other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.filter(col("a").ge(2))
method gt def gt(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise greater-than, like expr > other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.filter(col("a").gt(2))
method le def le(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise less-than-or-equal, like expr <= other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.filter(col("a").le(2))
method lt def lt(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise less-than, like expr < other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.filter(col("a").lt(2))

method ne def ne(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise inequality, equivalent to expr != other. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. A null on either side yields null; use ne_missing to treat two nulls as equal. Example: tf.filter(col("g").ne("x"))

method ne_missing def ne_missing(other: Any) -> Expr Element-wise inequality where two nulls compare as equal. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to compare against. Example: tf.select(col("v").ne_missing(None).alias("filled"))

method add def add(other: Any) -> Expr Add other; for strings, concatenate. Same as +. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to add or concatenate. Example: tf.with_columns(col("a").add(1).alias("next"))

method floordiv def floordiv(other: Any) -> Expr Floor division by other. Same as //. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to divide by. Example: tf.select(col("a").floordiv(2).alias("halved"))
method mod def mod(other: Any) -> Expr Modulo (remainder) by other. Same as %. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to divide by. Example: tf.select(col("a").mod(2).alias("parity"))
method mul def mul(other: Any) -> Expr Multiply by other. Same as *. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to multiply by. Example: tf.with_columns(col("a").mul(10).alias("scaled"))
method sub def sub(other: Any) -> Expr Subtract other. Same as -. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to subtract. Example: tf.with_columns(col("b").sub(col("a")).alias("gap"))
method neg def neg() -> Expr Unary negation of each element. Same as unary -. Example: tf.select(col("a").neg().alias("negated"))

method truediv def truediv(other: Any) -> Expr True (floating-point) division by other. Same as /. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to divide by. Example: tf.select(col("b").truediv(col("a")).alias("ratio"))

method pow def pow(exponent: IntoExprColumn | int | float) -> Expr Raise each element to the power of exponent. Same as **. Parameters: # parameter exponentIntoExprColumn | int | float (Expr | str | int | float) Value or expression to use as the exponent. Example: tf.select(col("a").pow(2).alias("squared"))

method xor def xor(other: Any) -> Expr Bitwise xor with other (integer or boolean). Same as ^. Parameters: # parameter otherAny Value or expression to combine with xor. Example: tf.select(col("flag").xor(True).alias("toggled"))

method is_in def is_in(other: Expr | Collection[Any], *, nulls_equal: bool = False) -> Expr Return whether each element is contained in other. Parameters: # parameter otherExpr | Collection[Any] Collection or expression of allowed values. # parameter nulls_equalbool If True, a null element matches a null in other. Example: tf.filter(col("g").is_in(["x", "y"]))

method is_between def is_between( lower_bound: IntoExpr, upper_bound: IntoExpr, closed: ClosedInterval = 'both', ) -> Expr Return whether each element lies between two bounds. Parameters: # parameter lower_boundIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Lower bound value or expression. # parameter upper_boundIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Upper bound value or expression. # parameter closedClosedInterval (Literal['left', 'right', 'both', 'none']) Which ends are inclusive: both (default), left, right or none. Example: tf.filter(col("a").is_between(2, 4)) Both bounds are inclusive by default; closed narrows them: tf.filter(col("a").is_between(2, 4, closed="left"))

method hash def hash( seed: int = 0, seed_1: int | None = None, seed_2: int | None = None, seed_3: int | None = None, ) -> Expr Hash each element to a 64-bit unsigned integer. Parameters: # parameter seedint Base seed for the hash. # parameter seed_1int | None Optional additional seed. # parameter seed_2int | None Optional additional seed. # parameter seed_3int | None Optional additional seed. Example: tf.select(col("email").hash().alias("fingerprint"))

method reinterpret def reinterpret( *, signed: bool | None = None, dtype: PolarsDataType | None = None, ) -> Expr Reinterpret a 64-bit integer's bits as another integer type. Reinterprets the raw bits (no value conversion); for a real conversion use cast. Only valid on 64-bit integer columns. Parameters: # parameter signedbool | None If True reinterpret as signed, if False as unsigned. # parameter dtypePolarsDataType | None (DataType | None) Explicit target integer type; overrides signed. Example: tf.select(col("a").reinterpret(signed=False).alias("bits"))
method abs def abs() -> Expr Absolute value of each element. Example: tf.select(col("v").abs().alias("size"))

method rank def rank( method: RankMethod = 'average', *, descending: bool = False, seed: int | None = None, ) -> Expr Assign a rank to each element within the column. Parameters: # parameter methodRankMethod (Literal['average', 'min', 'max', 'dense', 'ordinal', 'random']) Tie-handling method: average (default), min, max, dense, ordinal or random. # parameter descendingbool If True, rank from largest to smallest. # parameter seedint | None Random seed, used only when method is random. Example: tf.with_columns(col("a").rank().alias("position")) method decides how ties are resolved, and descending ranks the largest value first: tf.with_columns(col("a").rank("dense", descending=True).alias("place"))

method diff def diff(n: int | IntoExpr = 1, null_behavior: NullBehavior = 'ignore') -> Expr Difference between each element and one n rows away. Works on numeric and temporal columns. Order-dependent, so sort first for a deterministic result. Parameters: # parameter nint | IntoExpr (int | int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Rows to look back; negative looks forward. # parameter null_behaviorNullBehavior (Literal['ignore', 'drop']) How to handle nulls: ignore or drop. Example: tf.sort("id").with_columns(col("a").diff().alias("change"))

method clip def clip( lower_bound: NumericLiteral | TemporalLiteral | IntoExprColumn | None = None, upper_bound: NumericLiteral | TemporalLiteral | IntoExprColumn | None = None, ) -> Expr Clamp each element to the given bounds. Values below lower_bound become it, values above upper_bound become it, values in range are unchanged. Provide at least one bound. Parameters: # parameter lower_boundNumericLiteral | TemporalLiteral | IntoExprColumn | None (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | Expr | str | None) Minimum allowed value; None for no lower bound. # parameter upper_boundNumericLiteral | TemporalLiteral | IntoExprColumn | None (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | Expr | str | None) Maximum allowed value; None for no upper bound. Example: tf.with_columns(col("a").clip(2, 3).alias("clipped")) One bound may be omitted to clamp on a single side: tf.with_columns(col("a").clip(lower_bound=2).alias("at_least_two"))

TableFrame class class TableFrame Bases: EngineFrame Categories: tableframe A lazy, immutable tabular frame -- Tabsdata's wrapper over polars LazyFrame. Every operation returns a new TableFrame without mutating the input. Instances arrive as arguments (and are returned) in @publisher / @transformer / @subscriber functions; build one directly with TableFrame.from_polars / from_pandas / from_dict / empty. Reference columns with col and constants with lit (both from tabsdatak.tableframe.functions).

class class TableFrame Bases: EngineFrame Categories: tableframe A lazy, immutable tabular frame -- Tabsdata's wrapper over polars LazyFrame. Every operation returns a new TableFrame without mutating the input. Instances arrive as arguments (and are returned) in @publisher / @transformer / @subscriber functions; build one directly with TableFrame.from_polars / from_pandas / from_dict / empty. Reference columns with col and constants with lit (both from tabsdatak.tableframe.functions).
tf = TableFrame.from_dict({"g": ["x", "y", "x"], "v": [1, 2, 3]}) tf.filter(col("v") > 1).group_by("g").agg(col("v").sum().alias("total"))

method explain def explain( *, format: ExplainFormat = 'plain', optimized: bool = True, type_coercion: bool = True, predicate_pushdown: bool = True, projection_pushdown: bool = True, simplify_expression: bool = True, slice_pushdown: bool = True, comm_subplan_elim: bool = True, comm_subexpr_elim: bool = True, cluster_with_columns: bool = True, collapse_joins: bool = True, streaming: bool = False, engine: EngineType = 'auto', tree_format: bool | None = None, optimizations: Any = ..., ) -> str Return the query plan of this TableFrame as text. The remaining boolean flags each toggle one query-plan optimization (predicate/projection pushdown, common-subplan elimination, ...); leave them at their defaults unless diagnosing the plan. Parameters: # parameter formatExplainFormat (Literal['plain', 'tree']) "plain" or "tree" rendering. # parameter optimizedbool Show the optimized plan (default) rather than the raw logical plan. # parameter type_coercionbool # parameter predicate_pushdownbool # parameter projection_pushdownbool # parameter simplify_expressionbool # parameter slice_pushdownbool # parameter comm_subplan_elimbool # parameter comm_subexpr_elimbool # parameter cluster_with_columnsbool # parameter collapse_joinsbool # parameter streamingbool Show the plan for streaming execution. # parameter engineEngineType (Literal['auto', 'in-memory', 'streaming', 'gpu']) Target engine -- "auto", "in-memory", "streaming" or "gpu". # parameter tree_formatbool | None # parameter optimizationsAny Example: tf.filter(col("a") > 2).explain() The tree rendering is easier to read for a deep plan: tf.explain(format="tree")

method show_graph def show_graph( *, optimized: bool = True, show: bool = True, output_path: str | Path | None = None, raw_output: bool = False, figsize: tuple[float, float] = (16.0, 12.0), type_coercion: bool = True, _type_check: bool = True, predicate_pushdown: bool = True, projection_pushdown: bool = True, simplify_expression: bool = True, slice_pushdown: bool = True, comm_subplan_elim: bool = True, comm_subexpr_elim: bool = True, cluster_with_columns: bool = True, collapse_joins: bool = True, engine: EngineType = 'auto', plan_stage: PlanStage = 'ir', _check_order: bool = True, optimizations: Any = ..., ) -> str | None Render the query plan of this TableFrame as a graph. The remaining boolean flags toggle individual query-plan optimizations; leave them at their defaults unless diagnosing the plan. Parameters: # parameter optimizedbool Graph the optimized plan (default) rather than the raw logical plan. # parameter showbool Display the graph (needs Graphviz); set False to only return or write it. # parameter output_pathstr | Path | None If given, write the rendered graph to this path. # parameter raw_outputbool Return the raw DOT string instead of rendering. # parameter figsizetuple[float, float] Figure size as (width, height) in inches. # parameter type_coercionbool # parameter _type_checkbool # parameter predicate_pushdownbool # parameter projection_pushdownbool # parameter simplify_expressionbool # parameter slice_pushdownbool # parameter comm_subplan_elimbool # parameter comm_subexpr_elimbool # parameter cluster_with_columnsbool # parameter collapse_joinsbool # parameter engineEngineType (Literal['auto', 'in-memory', 'streaming', 'gpu']) # parameter plan_stagePlanStage (Literal['ir', 'physical']) # parameter _check_orderbool # parameter optimizationsAny Example: tf.show_graph() # opens the rendered plan; needs Graphviz Skip the viewer and take the DOT source instead: tf.show_graph(show=False, raw_output=True)

method inspect def inspect(fmt: str = '{}') -> TableFrame Print this TableFrame mid-chain and pass it through unchanged. Handy for debugging a chained pipeline: it returns the same TableFrame so it can sit between other operations. Parameters: # parameter fmtstr Format string applied to the printed frame. Example: tf.filter(col("a") > 1).inspect().select("a", "b")

method sort def sort( by: IntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr], *more_by: IntoExpr = (), descending: bool | Sequence[bool] = False, nulls_last: bool | Sequence[bool] = False, maintain_order: bool = False, multithreaded: bool = True, ) -> TableFrame Sort the rows by one or more columns or expressions. Parameters: # parameter byIntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Iterable[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None]) Column name(s) or expression(s) to sort by. # parameter *more_byIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Additional sort keys, as positional arguments. # parameter descendingbool | Sequence[bool] Sort descending; a single bool, or one per sort key. # parameter nulls_lastbool | Sequence[bool] Place nulls last; a single bool, or one per sort key. # parameter maintain_orderbool Keep the input order of tied rows. # parameter multithreadedbool Example: tf.sort("k", descending=True) tf.sort(["k", "n"], descending=[True, False])

method cast def cast( dtypes: Mapping[ColumnNameOrSelector | PolarsDataType, PolarsDataType | PythonDataType] | PolarsDataType | Schema, *, strict: bool = True, ) -> TableFrame Cast columns to new data types. Data types come from tabsdatak.tableframe.datatypes. Parameters: # parameter dtypesMapping[ColumnNameOrSelector | PolarsDataType, PolarsDataType | PythonDataType] | PolarsDataType | Schema (Mapping[str | Any | DataType, DataType | type[int] | type[float] | type[bool] | type[str] | type[date] | type[time] | type[datetime] | type[timedelta] | type[list[Any]] | type[tuple[Any, ...]] | type[bytes] | type[object] | type[Decimal] | type[None]] | DataType | Schema) A single data type applied to every column, a mapping of column (name or selector) to its target data type, or a Schema. # parameter strictbool If True (default), raise when a value cannot be cast; if False, unconvertible values become null. Example: tf.cast({"a": Float64, "b": String}) tf.cast({"id": Int8}, strict=False)

method clear def clear(n: int = 0) -> TableFrame Return a frame with the same schema but no data. Parameters: # parameter nint Number of all-null rows to produce. 0 (default) yields a zero-row frame; a positive n yields n rows of nulls. Example: tf.clear() A positive n keeps the schema and yields that many all-null rows: tf.clear(3)

method filter def filter( *predicates: IntoExprColumn | Iterable[IntoExprColumn] | bool | list[bool] = (), **constraints: Any = {}, ) -> TableFrame Keep only the rows matching every given predicate. Parameters: # parameter *predicatesIntoExprColumn | Iterable[IntoExprColumn] | bool | list[bool] (Expr | str | Iterable[Expr | str] | bool | list[bool]) Boolean expressions; a row is kept only if it satisfies ALL of them (they are AND-ed together). # parameter **constraintsAny Column-equality shortcuts as keyword arguments -- filter(g="x") means filter(col("g") == "x"). Example: tf.filter(col("a") > 2) tf.filter((col("a") > 1) & (col("a") < 5)) tf.filter(col("g").is_in(["x", "y"])) tf.filter(g="x")

method select def select( *exprs: IntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] = (), **named_exprs: IntoExpr = {}, ) -> TableFrame Select and/or derive columns, dropping every other column. Parameters: # parameter *exprsIntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Iterable[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None]) Column names or expressions to keep; each expression becomes a column (name it with Expr.alias). # parameter **named_exprsIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Expressions as keyword arguments, where the keyword is the output column name. Example: tf.select("a", "b") tf.select((col("a") * 2).alias("a2")) tf.select(a2=col("a") * 2)

method group_by def group_by( *by: IntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] = (), maintain_order: bool = False, **named_by: IntoExpr = {}, ) -> LazyGroupBy Group rows by one or more keys for aggregation. Returns a LazyGroupBy; call .agg(...) on it with reducing expressions to produce one row per group. Prefer agg(col(...).<reduction>()) over the LazyGroupBy reduction shortcuts (see LazyGroupBy). Parameters: # parameter *byIntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Iterable[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None]) Column name(s) or expression(s) to group by. # parameter maintain_orderbool Emit groups in the order they first appear. # parameter **named_byIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Grouping expressions as keyword arguments, where the keyword names the group column. Example: tf.group_by("k").agg(col("v").sum().alias("s"))

method join def join( other: TableFrame, on: str | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None = None, how: JoinStrategy = 'inner', *, left_on: str | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None = None, right_on: str | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None = None, suffix: str = '_right', ) -> TableFrame Join this TableFrame with another on one or more keys. #MANUAL CHANGE POST GEN: dropped the generated params validate, nulls_equal, coalesce, maintain_order, allow_parallel, force_parallel -- the runtime does not accept them (TypeError). Parameters: # parameter otherTableFrame The right TableFrame to join with. # parameter onstr | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None Key column(s) present in BOTH frames. Use this OR left_on/right_on, never both; omit it for how="cross". # parameter howJoinStrategy (Literal['inner', 'left', 'right', 'full', 'semi', 'anti', 'cross', 'outer']) Join strategy -- one of "inner", "left", "right", "full" (a.k.a. "outer"), "cross", "semi" or "anti". "semi" keeps left rows that have a match, "anti" keeps those that do not, and "cross" is the cartesian product (takes no keys). # parameter left_onstr | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None Key column(s) on the left frame, paired positionally with right_on when the join keys have different names. # parameter right_onstr | Expr | Sequence[str | Expr] | None Key column(s) on the right frame; use with left_on. # parameter suffixstr Suffix added to right-frame columns whose names collide with the left frame (default "_right"). Example: left.join(right, on="id", how="inner") left.join(right, left_on="id", right_on="rid") left.join(right, how="cross")

method with_columns def with_columns( *exprs: IntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] = (), **named_exprs: IntoExpr = {}, ) -> TableFrame Add or replace columns, keeping all existing ones. Like select but non-destructive: the given expressions are added, and any whose name matches an existing column replaces it in place. Parameters: # parameter *exprsIntoExpr | Iterable[IntoExpr] (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Iterable[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None]) Expressions to add; name each with Expr.alias. # parameter **named_exprsIntoExpr (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None) Expressions as keyword arguments, where the keyword is the output column name. Example: tf.with_columns((col("a") + 1).alias("c")) tf.with_columns(c=col("a") + col("b"))

method drop def drop( *columns: ColumnNameOrSelector | Iterable[ColumnNameOrSelector] = (), strict: bool = True, ) -> TableFrame Remove the named columns. Parameters: # parameter *columnsColumnNameOrSelector | Iterable[ColumnNameOrSelector] (str | Any | Iterable[str | Any]) Column name(s) or selector(s) to drop, as several positional arguments or a single list. # parameter strictbool If True (default), raise when a named column is missing; if False, silently ignore missing names. Example: tf.drop("a", "b") tf.drop(["b", "c"])

method rename def rename( mapping: Mapping[str, str] | Callable[[str], str], *, strict: bool = True, ) -> TableFrame Rename columns. #VERIFY: the callable form (a function over column names) has a known system-column divergence (xp failing sub-suite); the dict form is the reliable one. Parameters: # parameter mappingMapping[str, str] | Callable[[str], str] A dict of {old_name: new_name} (the reliable form), or a callable applied to each existing column name to produce its new name. # parameter strictbool If True (default), raise when a key in mapping is not an existing column. Example: tf.rename({"a": "x", "b": "y"})

method slice def slice(offset: int, length: int | None = None) -> TableFrame Return length rows starting at row offset. Parameters: # parameter offsetint Zero-based index of the first row to keep. # parameter lengthint | None Number of rows to keep; None keeps all rows from offset to the end. Example: tf.slice(1, 2) # two rows, starting at the second Omit the length to take everything from offset on: tf.slice(2)
method limit def limit(n: int = 5) -> TableFrame Return the first n rows (an alias of head). Parameters: # parameter nint Number of rows to keep. Example: tf.limit(3)
method head def head(n: int = 5) -> TableFrame Return the first n rows. Parameters: # parameter nint Number of rows to keep. Example: tf.head(3)
method tail def tail(n: int = 5) -> TableFrame Return the last n rows. Parameters: # parameter nint Number of rows to keep. Example: tf.tail(3)
method last def last() -> TableFrame Return the last row as a one-row TableFrame. Example: tf.sort("id").last()
method first def first() -> TableFrame Return the first row as a one-row TableFrame. Example: tf.sort("id").first()

method fill_null def fill_null( value: Any | Expr | None = None, strategy: FillNullStrategy | None = None, limit: int | None = None, *, matches_supertype: bool = True, ) -> TableFrame Replace null values with a value or a fill strategy. Provide either value or strategy, not both. Parameters: # parameter valueAny | Expr | None Value (or expression) to substitute for nulls. # parameter strategyFillNullStrategy | None (Literal['forward', 'backward', 'min', 'max', 'mean', 'zero', 'one'] | None) Fill rule instead of a value -- one of "forward", "backward", "min", "max", "mean", "zero" or "one". # parameter limitint | None With "forward" / "backward", the maximum number of consecutive nulls to fill. # parameter matches_supertypebool Cast the fill value to the column's supertype when their types differ. Example: tf.fill_null(0) tf.sort("id").fill_null(strategy="forward", limit=1)

method fill_nan def fill_nan(value: int | float | Expr | None) -> TableFrame Replace floating-point NaN values with the given value. Targets NaN entries in float columns -- distinct from fill_null, which replaces nulls. Parameters: # parameter valueint | float | Expr | None Value (or expression) to substitute for NaN. Example: tf.fill_nan(0.0)

method unique def unique( subset: IntoExpr | Collection[IntoExpr] | None = None, *, keep: UniqueKeepStrategy = 'any', maintain_order: bool = False, ) -> TableFrame Remove duplicate rows. #VERIFY: omitting subset (dedup on all columns) has a known system-column divergence (xp failing sub-suite); pass subset explicitly. Parameters: # parameter subsetIntoExpr | Collection[IntoExpr] | None (int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None | Collection[int | float | Decimal | date | time | datetime | timedelta | str | bool | bytes | list[Any] | Expr | str | None] | None) Column(s) whose values define a duplicate; pass this explicitly. When omitted, all columns are considered. # parameter keepUniqueKeepStrategy (Literal['first', 'last', 'any', 'none']) Which duplicate to keep -- "any" (default, fastest), "first", "last" or "none" (drop every duplicated row). # parameter maintain_orderbool Preserve the input row order. Example: tf.unique(subset="a") tf.unique(subset="k", keep="last")

method drop_nans def drop_nans( subset: ColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector] | None = None, ) -> TableFrame Drop rows containing floating-point NaN values. Parameters: # parameter subsetColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector] | None (str | Any | Collection[str | Any] | None) Column(s) to check for NaN; when omitted, all columns are considered. Example: tf.drop_nans("v") Omit the subset to drop a row when any float column holds NaN: tf.drop_nans()

method drop_nulls def drop_nulls( subset: ColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector] | None = None, ) -> TableFrame Drop rows containing null values. Parameters: # parameter subsetColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector] | None (str | Any | Collection[str | Any] | None) Column(s) to check for nulls; when omitted, all columns are considered. Example: tf.drop_nulls("v") Omit the subset to drop a row when any column is null: tf.drop_nulls()

method unnest def unnest( columns: ColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector], *more_columns: ColumnNameOrSelector = (), separator: str | None = None, ) -> TableFrame Expand struct columns into one column per field. Each named struct column is replaced, in place, by its fields as top-level columns. Parameters: # parameter columnsColumnNameOrSelector | Collection[ColumnNameOrSelector] (str | Any | Collection[str | Any]) Struct column(s) to expand. # parameter *more_columnsColumnNameOrSelector (str | Any) Additional struct columns, as positional arguments. # parameter separatorstr | None If given, prefix each new column with its parent name and this separator to avoid name clashes. Example: tf.unnest("s") tf.unnest("s", "t")

method grok def grok( expr: str | Expr, pattern: str, schema: Mapping[str, ColumnDefinition], ) -> TableFrame Parse unstructured text into columns with a Grok pattern. Matches pattern against a string column and appends one column per named capture, keeping every existing column. A row whose text does not match gets null in each new column, so a bad line never fails the read. ColumnDefinition (from tabsdatak.tableframe.grok) names each new column and gives its data type. Parameters: # parameter exprstr | Expr Name of the string column to parse, or an expression resolving to one. # parameter patternstr Grok pattern whose named captures (%{WORD:user}) become the new columns. # parameter schemaMapping[str, ColumnDefinition] Mapping of capture name to the ColumnDefinition describing the column it produces. A definition whose name differs from the capture renames the output column; its dtype is what the captured text is parsed into. Returns: A new TableFrame with one column added per capture. Example: tf.grok( "logs", r"%{WORD:user}-%{WORD:action}-%{INT:year}", { "user": ColumnDefinition("user", String), "action": ColumnDefinition("action", String), "year": ColumnDefinition("year", Int64), }, ) A definition can rename the capture, and the source column may be given as an expression: tf.grok( col("logs"), r"%{WORD:user}-.*", {"user": ColumnDefinition("who", String)}, ) When a pattern repeats a capture name, the extra columns are disambiguated with a numeric suffix (field, field[1]).

method from_polars def from_polars(data = None, schema = None) -> TableFrame Build a TableFrame from a polars frame. Takes a polars DataFrame or LazyFrame; any other input type raises. The system columns are seeded on top of the given data. Parameters: # parameter data The polars DataFrame or LazyFrame to wrap. None yields an empty frame. # parameter schema Optional {column: data type} mapping to cast the data to; the data keeps its own types when omitted. Returns: A new TableFrame over the given data. Example: TableFrame.from_polars(pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})) TableFrame.from_polars(pl.LazyFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]}))

method from_pandas def from_pandas(data = None, schema = None) -> TableFrame Build a TableFrame from a pandas DataFrame. Parameters: # parameter data The pandas DataFrame to convert. None yields an empty frame. # parameter schema Optional {column: data type} mapping to cast the data to; the types pandas inferred are kept when omitted. Returns: A new TableFrame over the given data. Example: TableFrame.from_pandas(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]}))

method from_dict def from_dict(data = None, schema = None) -> TableFrame Build a TableFrame from a {column: values} dict. Every value list must have the same length -- one entry per row. Parameters: # parameter data Mapping of column name to the column's values. None yields an empty frame. # parameter schema Optional {column: data type} mapping to cast the columns to; types are inferred from the values when omitted. Returns: A new TableFrame over the given data. Example: TableFrame.from_dict({"g": ["x", "y"], "v": [1, 2]}) Pin the column types instead of having them inferred: TableFrame.from_dict({"v": [1, 2]}, schema={"v": Float64})

method empty def empty(schema = None) -> TableFrame Build a TableFrame with no rows. Parameters: # parameter schema Optional {column: data type} mapping giving the frame its columns. Without it the frame has no columns either. Returns: A new, empty TableFrame. Example: TableFrame.empty(schema={"id": Int64, "name": String}) With no schema the result has neither rows nor columns -- useful as the starting point of a concat: TableFrame.empty()

method to_polars_lf def to_polars_lf(drop_system_columns = True) Return the underlying polars LazyFrame, unevaluated. This leaves the TableFrame API: the result is a plain polars frame that no longer carries the system columns or the lazy bookkeeping around them. Parameters: # parameter drop_system_columns Remove the internal $td.* columns (the default). Pass False to keep them. Returns: The polars LazyFrame behind this TableFrame. Example: tf.to_polars_lf()
